bib.title: MemFactory: Unified Inference & Training Framework for Agent Memory

legacy_report:
**COVERAGE:** 10 of 10 pages, 32,164 chars, including the references. There are no appendices. The extraction was clean.

**TITLE:** MemFactory: Unified Inference & Training Framework for Agent Memory (arXiv 2603.29493v4, cs.CL).
**AUTHORS:** Ziliang Guo, Ziheng Li, Bo Tang, Feiyu Xiong, Zhiyu Li (corresponding author).
- The only affiliation on the extracted page is MemTensor.
- The correspondence email is lizy@memtensor.cn.
- Code: github.com/MemTensor/MemFactory.

**VENUE/DATE:** Preprint, dated April 8, 2026 on the title page. The arXiv stamp says v4, 7 Apr 2026.

**MAIN CLAIM:** This is an infrastructure paper, not a new memory-RL method. MemFactory is a modular framework with four layers: Module, Agent, Environment and Trainer. Memory operations (extract, update, retrieve, plus an end-to-end Agent Module) are split into plug-in components. A built-in GRPO trainer optimises them. It ships three agents that re-implement earlier work: MemoryR1Agent (Memory-R1), MemoryAgent (MemAgent) and MemoryRMMAgent (RMM). Only MemoryAgent is tested empirically.

**HEADLINE NUMBERS** (Table 2, p7)

All scores are the MemAgent recurrent-memory agent, avg@4 (four trials per question). Training ran 250 valid steps on one A800 80GB GPU. Training samples were shortened to about one-third of the original length (50–80 documents). The test sets are eval_50 and eval_100 (main task) and eval_fwe_16384 (out of distribution). The paper does not state the number of questions per set.
1. Qwen3-1.7B average rose from 0.3118 to 0.3581, a relative gain of 14.8%. This is the "up to 14.8%" in the abstract.
   - eval_50: 0.4727 to 0.5684.
   - eval_100: 0.4297 to 0.4863.
   - OOD: 0.0332 to 0.0195, a drop.
2. Qwen3-4B-Instruct average rose from 0.6146 to 0.6595, a relative gain of 7.3%.
   - eval_50: 0.6523 to 0.7051.
   - eval_100: 0.5645 to 0.6309.
   - OOD: 0.6270 to 0.6426.
3. The baseline is the same base checkpoint, untrained. There is no comparison with the original MemAgent training recipe or with other methods.

**QUOTES**
- p7: "For Qwen3-1.7B, the framework achieves a relative increase of 14.8% in the average score. This is driven primarily by strong gains in the main-task settings, although performance on the OOD benchmark slightly decreases."
- p3: Memory-R1 "trains a Memory Manager to execute discrete CRUD operations (e.g., ADD, UPDATE, DELETE) and an Answer Agent for memory distillation… exact-match rewards are sufficient to teach sophisticated memory consolidation without dense human annotation." This is the authors' summary of Memory-R1, not a result of their own.

**LIMITS**
- The authors concede (p8) that the framework covers "only a limited set of representative paradigms" and leaves "room for further improvement in training efficiency".
- Memory-R1 and RMM are provided but never trained or evaluated, so the paper gives no evidence that the framework reproduces Memory-R1's results.
- The paper reports no seeds, variance or significance tests, and no ablations.
- The 1.7B out-of-distribution score fell from 0.0332 to 0.0195. The text says it "slightly decreases". The base score was near zero.
- The claim that the larger model "effectively transfers" the policy rests on one OOD set.
- The training data was simplified (context cut to about one-third), and no comparison against the original MemAgent numbers is given.
- Rewards are described only as format rewards and LLM-as-a-Judge. The paper does not say which reward each experiment used.
- "First unified framework" is the authors' own claim.

**BUILDS ON**
- Memory-R1 (Yan et al., arXiv 2508.19828; the reference list says 2026).
- MemAgent (Yu et al., 2025, arXiv 2507.02259; uses Multi-Conversation DAPO).
- RMM (Tan et al., 2025, arXiv 2503.08026; uses REINFORCE).
- MemAct (Zhang et al., 2026).
- GRPO (Shao et al., 2024, DeepSeekMath).
- PPO (Schulman et al., 2017).
- LLaMA-Factory (Zheng et al., 2024).
- VERL/HybridFlow (Sheng et al., EuroSys 2025).
- MS-Swift (Zhao et al., AAAI 2025).
- MemOS (Li et al., 2025).
- Mem0 (Chhikara et al., 2025).
- MemEngine (Zhang et al., 2025).
- The memory survey "Memory in the Age of AI Agents" (Hu et al., 2026).

**FIGURE CANDIDATE:** Figure 1 (p4) shows the four-layer architecture. Modules (Extractor, Updater, Retriever, Agent Module) sit under the Agent Layer. The Environment Layer holds the data loader and reward manager. The Trainer Layer holds the GRPO engine with advantage computation, KL penalty and policy update. It is a box diagram only, with no results. Table 1 (p5) lists the three module interfaces: generate, rollout and inference.

**FOR THE NOTE:** The paper sharpens the Memory-R1 section only as a pointer. The Updater's four operations are ADD, DEL, UPDATE and NONE (p5), and GRPO advantage is the intra-group normalisation in Eq. 1 (p4). It adds no new Memory-R1 evidence. The only measured result is for MemAgent-style recurrent memory, not for CRUD-style memory.

**PROBLEMS:** None. The PDF contains no embedded instructions. The extracted text is at /tmp/mf.txt.
